content:
- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes in history (e.g., 75+ values) — model reacts too aggressively, peaking too high then falling.
- Underestimates downward trends or corrections — fails to recognize when prices are trending lower, especially after 70–72 range.
- Mean reversion bias: model holds too much upward momentum, ignoring recent price pullbacks toward 70–71.
- Lagged response: model reacts to recent history with delay — e.g., 70s dip in history is not reflected in forecast until 3–5 days later.
- Overconfidence in short-term volatility — forecasts show erratic swings without anchoring to recent 30-day mean.
- Avoids “reversion to mean” behavior — fails to adjust forecast toward historical average when price deviates >10% from 30-day mean.
- High sensitivity to recent spikes — model amplifies recent highs (e.g., 75+), then overcorrects downward, missing intermediate dips.
- Underestimates downward momentum after 70–72 range — model assumes continuation of upward trend when price is consolidating or declining.
